title: Detailed Cerebral Organoid Fusion Method
protocol: Culture hiPSCs in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Maintain feeder-dependent hiPSCs on gelatin-coated 0.1% wt/vol 6-well Eppendorf plates containing pre-plated MEFs at 1.87x10^5 cells/well.
Feed hPSCs daily with 2 mL of hES media containing 20 ng/mL bFGF.
Passage hiPSCs using 0.1% wt/vol collagenase IV in DMEM-F12 medium for 5–10 min.
Scrape intact colonies with a cell lifter and triturate with a 1-ml pipette tip to obtain smaller colonies before plating.
Maintain feeder-free hESCs in mTeSR1 on Matrigel-coated plates.
Dissolve low-growth-factor Matrigel in ice-cold DMEM-F12 using a volume containing 0.5 mg of Matrigel per plate.
Passage feeder-independent hESCs using 0.5 mM EDTA in sterile D-PBS without calcium and magnesium.
Mix 400 mL DMEM/F12, 100 mL KOSR, 15 mL FBS, 5 mL Glutamax, 5 mL of MEM-NEAA, and 3.5 µL of 2-ME to prepare hES media for 500 mL volume.
Sterile filter the prepared medium using a 22 µm filter bottle.
Add FGF2 or bFGF and RI just before usage.
Store the medium at 4°C for up to 2 weeks after preparation.
Mix 500 mL DMEM/F12, 5 mL N2 supplement, 5 mL GlutaMAX, 5 mL MEM-NEAA, and 500 µL heparin solution to prepare NI media for 500 mL volume.
Sterile filter the prepared medium using a 22 µm filter bottle.
Store the medium at 4°C for up to 2 weeks after preparation.

Mix 250ml DMEM/F12 with 250ml Neurobasal, 2.5ml N2 supplement, 5ml B27 \(with or without vitamin A), 125µl Insulin, 175µl of a 1:100 solution of 2-ME in DMEM/F12, 5ml Glutamax, 2.5ml MEM-NEAA and 5ml Penicillin+Streptomycin solution to prepare differentiation media.
Sterile filter the prepared differentiation media using a 22µm filter bottle.
Add thawed Matrigel to ice cold Diff-A media after sterile filtering for use with Matrigel.
Store medium at 4°C for up to 2 weeks after preparation.
Reconstitute 50μg bFGF in 5ml PBS +0.1% BSA to prepare a 10µg/ml bFGF stock solution.
Aliquot the prepared bFGF stock solution into appropriate volumes and store at -20°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare a heparin stock solution by dissolving 1 mg in PBS to make a 1 mg/ml solution.
Store the heparin stock solution at -20°C for up to 1 year.
Reconstitute 5mg Rock Inhibitor \(RI) in 2.96 mL of H2O to prepare a working solution.
Aliquot the RI working solution into 0.5-1ml portions and store at -20°C.
Count the cell density of the single-cell suspension using a Countess cell counter.
Combine 6 µL of the cell suspension with 6 µL of Trypan Blue.
Load 10 µL into the counting slides.
Add 9000 live cells in 150 µL of hES media + bFGF, +RI to each well of a 96-well low-attachment U-bottom cell culture plate.
Create a master mix by combining all the cells required for the total number of wells.
Calculate 100 wells per 96 well plate and combine 900,000 live cells in 15 mL media.
Pipette 150 µL of this solution into each well using a p200 pipetman or multichannel pipet.
Exchange the media by removing ~75% of the media in each well on Day 3.
Add 150 µL of fresh hES media (without bFGF or RI) to each well.
Remove ~75% of the media when EBs are >500 µm in diameter on Day 5.
Replace with neural induction (NI) media containing no small molecules for stabilizing a dorsal identity, add 1:1000 cyclopamine A (CycA) stock to the NI medium.
Replace with neural induction (NI) media and add 1:2000 IWP2 stock and 1:10,000 SAG stock for promoting a ventral identity.
Exchange the media by removing ~75% of the media in each well and adding 150 µL of fresh NI media containing the desired small molecule patterning treatments.
Thaw matrigel on ice, and maintain on ice throughout the embedding procedure.
Transfer EBs from the 96-well U-bottom plate into a 6 cm Eppendorf cell culture dish containing 3 mL of Differentiation medium \(- Vit. A) using a p200 with a widened tip cut with scissors.
Prepare parafilm wells by pressing a piece of parafilm onto the top of an empty p200 pipet tip box.
Transfer the sheet of parafilm wells to a cell culture dish.
Transfer 1 dorsal and 1 ventral EB into each parafilm well using a p200 with a widened tip.
Carefully remove the excess media surrounding the EBs using a p200 pipetman.
Embed organoids in a droplet of Matrigel using a p200 pipetman.
Place the pipet tip against the bottom of the parafilm well next to the EBs to form the droplet.
Gently position the EBs in the middle of the matrigel droplet using a p200 pipet tip.
Push dorsal and ventral EBs as close to each other as possible using a p200 pipet tip.
Place the dish of embedded EBs into a 37°C incubator for 20 minutes to solidify the matrigel.
Add differentiation medium to gently wash the embedded EBs off the parafilm.
Remove the parafilm sheet and discard.
Place the embedded EBs onto a shelf in a 37°C cell culture incubator.
Exchange the media by removing approximately 75% of the media using a vacuum pump.
Add fresh differentiation (+Vit. A) medium to the dish.
Transfer the dish to an orbital shaker in a 37°C cell culture incubator.
Exchange the media twice a week with differentiation medium (+Vit. A).
Add 1% thawed matrigel to ice cold differentiation media.
Exchange the media twice a week with differentiation media (+Vit. A) containing 1% matrigel.
Prepare 4% low melt agarose in sterile PBS.
Heat the solution in a microwave and maintain melted agarose solution while stirring on a heat block at 60-70°C.
Transfer 1 mL aliquots of heated low-melt agarose solution into a heat-block set to 45°C.
Transfer organoid fusions from a cell culture dish into a tissue embedding mold using a widened p1000 tip cut with scissors and a pipetman.
Remove excess media surrounding the organoid fusion tissue.
Add 1 mL of 45°C low melt agarose solution into the tissue embedding mold.
Position the organoid fusion tissue in the center of the agarose, at the bottom of the tissue embedding mold.
Position the fusion tissue so that the two fusion tissue components (dorsal/ventral) are parallel to the base of the mold.
Add 1-2 mL of 45°C low melt agarose solution to the mold.
Chill the mold on a slurry of ice to quickly solidify the agarose embedded organoid fusion tissue.
Remove the agarose embedded tissue from the mold and attach it to the tissue holder plate of the vibratome chamber using super glue.
Fill the vibratome sectioning chamber with ice cold PBS (without Ca2+/Mg2+).
Section the organoid fusion tissue into 150-250 µm sections using maximum blade frequency and a slow speed setting (#4).
Immediately transfer the tissue sections to a 60 mm cell culture dish containing differentiation (+Vit. A.) medium.
Visibly inspect the sections under a microscope to determine which contain continuous tissue from both components of the organoid fusion.
Transfer these selected sections individually to an organotypic cell culture insert.
Place the cell culture insert into 1 mL of differentiation medium containing 5% FBS in a well of a 6-well Eppendorf cell culture plate.
Carefully remove any excess media from the top of the culture insert to ensure the tissue section rests directly on the membrane.
Replace the media with 1 mL of differentiation medium without FBS after Day 1.
Replace the media every other day starting from Days 3 until the slice cultures are desired for analyses.
